skill.name: improve
skill.description: Analyze a codebase as a senior advisor, identify high-value improvement opportunities, and write self-contained implementation plans for another agent or developer to execute.
skill.summary: Create prioritized codebase improvement plans without directly changing source code.
skill.author: shadcn

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, examples, and defensive audit guidance rather than executable code. The skill is intentionally read-only for source code, includes safeguards for secrets and prompt injection, and gates outward-facing issue publication behind explicit user confirmation. No evidence of malicious intent, credential exfiltration, hidden command execution, or unsafe prompt injection was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger many static command-execution patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Consider marking command examples and plan templates as documentation-only or moving risky-looking examples into clearly labeled reference sections to reduce marketplace scanner noise.

remediation.issue: The execute and --issues variants are powerful enough to affect worktrees or public issue trackers when explicitly invoked.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the existing isolation and confirmation requirements, and document them prominently in marketplace-facing descriptions.

content.value_statement: Teams often know a repository needs improvement but lack a clear, verified execution plan. This skill surveys the codebase, prioritizes evidence-backed findings, and writes plans that another agent can execute safely.
actual_capabilities: Maps repository structure, conventions, verification commands, and current development signals.
Audits code across correctness, security, performance, tests, architecture, dependencies, tooling, docs, and product direction.
Uses read-only exploration and subagents when available to gather evidence across large repositories.
Prioritizes findings by impact, effort, fix risk, and confidence before recommending plans.
Writes self-contained plan files with scope, steps, verification gates, done criteria, and stop conditions.
Can review or reconcile existing plans and, when supported, dispatch an isolated executor for a selected plan.
limitations: It is designed not to edit source code directly during the advisory workflow.
Large monorepos may still require scoped audits even at the deepest effort level.
Findings depend on readable local files and may miss behavior only visible in production telemetry.
Publishing plans as issues requires explicit user approval, especially for sensitive security findings.

use_cases.title: Prioritize technical debt work
use_cases.description: Find high-leverage refactors, test gaps, and architecture cleanup work with concrete evidence and execution order.

use_cases.title: Prepare safe agent handoffs
use_cases.description: Turn a vague improvement goal into a detailed plan that a lower-cost executor model can follow without session context.

use_cases.title: Review a branch before merge
use_cases.description: Audit changed files and related callers for introduced or pre-existing issues before implementation plans are written.

prompt_templates.title: Run a standard repository audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: get a broad improvement review and a small set of recommended plans.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use improve to audit this repository and recommend the top improvement plans. Keep the audit standard depth.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on one risk area
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: narrow the audit to security, performance, tests, or another category.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use improve with a security focus. Identify evidence-backed findings, reject false positives, and propose the highest-value plans.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a known change
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: skip broad discovery and produce one self-contained execution plan for a known goal.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use improve plan to specify how to migrate this package to the new API. Include exact files, verification gates, and stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit branch changes deeply
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review only current branch changes and classify issues as introduced or pre-existing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use improve branch deep. Audit changed files since the merge base, include related callers, and prepare plans for the top findings.

output_examples.input: Audit this repository for the best next improvements.
output: A prioritized findings table with evidence, impact, effort, risk, and confidence.
A recommendation for which findings should become implementation plans first.
A note about what was not audited or needs follow-up review.

output_examples.input: Create a plan for improving test coverage around payments.
output: A self-contained plan file with current-state evidence and explicit scope.
Step-by-step implementation guidance with verification commands after each stage.
Done criteria, stop conditions, and maintenance notes for the reviewer.

output_examples.input: Review an existing plan before another agent executes it.
output_examples.output: A critique of missing context, ambiguous steps, unsafe scope, weak verification, and suggested plan edits.

best_practices: Run the skill from a clean repository state so findings and plans can cite the correct baseline.
Choose a clear focus such as security, tests, performance, or branch review when time is limited.
Review sensitive findings before publishing plans or issues in a public repository.
anti_patterns: Do not ask this skill to make quick source edits; it is optimized for advisory planning.
Do not publish security plans as public issues without explicit review and confirmation.
Do not treat low-confidence direction ideas as mandatory roadmap items.

faq.question: Does this skill change my code?
faq.answer: No. The core workflow is read-only for source code and writes only plan files. The execute variant uses a separate isolated executor when available.

faq.question: What kinds of issues does it look for?
faq.answer: It reviews correctness, security, performance, tests, architecture, dependencies, developer experience, documentation, and product direction.

faq.question: Can it work on large monorepos?
faq.answer: Yes, but audits are scoped by effort level and may focus on key packages, hotspots, or user-selected areas.

faq.question: How are plans different from normal recommendations?
faq.answer: Plans include exact scope, current evidence, ordered steps, verification gates, done criteria, and stop conditions for another executor.

faq.question: Can it create GitHub issues?
faq.answer: Yes, only when the user uses the issues modifier. It requires extra confirmation before publishing sensitive findings in public repositories.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
